sections.h2: Where is the Onslow County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office is at 602 Anne Street in Jacksonville, NC 28540. Its mailing address is 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the main phone line is 910-347-3451.

Staff take recordings Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. The county directory lists marriage license hours as ending at 5:15 p.m. on the same days. Anyone selling a house in Onslow County will deal with this office at the end of the sale, because the deed to the buyer only counts against outsiders once it is filed here.

  • Walk-in address: 602 Anne Street, Jacksonville
  • Mail address: 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville
  • Phone: 910-347-3451, fax: 910-347-3340
  • Recording hours: 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday to Friday

sections.h2: What records does the Onslow County Register of Deeds keep?
sections.html:
The office holds real estate records that reach back to 1734. That file includes deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations of deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, separation agreements and road maintenance agreements.

Every real estate document filed there is public, and anyone can read it at the counter during office hours. Staff cannot fill in forms for you or run a title search, because North Carolina law bars them from the unauthorized practice of law. A seller who needs a title search should go to a closing attorney or a title company.

The county also lets people ask in writing to have a Social Security number, bank account number or similar personal data blacked out of an image shown on its public website. No fee is charged for that request.

sections.h2: What must an Onslow County deed show before the office will record it?
sections.html:
The first page has to state the excise tax amount, even when that amount is zero. Beyond that, Onslow County asks for a few specific items with each deed.

  • The excise tax figure printed on page one of the document, including a statement of zero where nothing is owed.
  • If the transfer is exempt by law, the reason for the exemption written on page one.
  • A Tax Certification Form attached to the back of the original deed. The county has required this since July 1, 2013 after a change approved by its Tax Office.
  • No Social Security, driver license, passport, bank account or card numbers in the body of the document, unless a law or court order requires them or only the last four digits appear.

A closing attorney normally checks these points before sending the deed to the office. If you are handling a signature yourself, call 910-347-3451 before you mail or hand over the original.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Onslow County?
sections.html:
North Carolina sets one fee schedule for every register of deeds, so Onslow County charges the same base amounts as any other county. The county page also lists charges of its own for extra instruments and card payments.

Recording fees in G.S. 161-10, charged by the Onslow office
DocumentFee as printed
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee

Onslow County adds $10 for each extra instrument in a single document, such as two papers that were signed and acknowledged separately and could each be recorded alone. Credit cards are taken for payments of $5 or more with a 3% processing fee added. The county links a current fee schedule from its Recording Information page, so check it before you send a check.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a house sale in Onslow County?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. State law puts the duty on the transferor, who pays the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

The rate printed on the Onslow County page is $1 on each $500, or fractional part of $500, of the price or value conveyed. The county directs readers to North Carolina General Statute 105-228.30 for the full rule. When two or more counties hold parts of one parcel, the tax goes to the county with the greater value. Half of what is collected stays with the county general fund and the other half goes to the Department of Revenue.

Because the tax comes out of the seller's side of the closing, it belongs on your net-proceeds worksheet. Ask your closing attorney for the exact figure on your price.

sections.h2: Why does the recording order matter when you sell an Onslow County house?
sections.html:
A deed or mortgage protects its holder against lien creditors and later buyers only from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies. State law ranks competing papers by the time they were filed.

That is why a closing is not final until the deed has actually reached the Onslow County office. Sellers who take a cash offer, sign a deed at a kitchen table, or hand a deed to a buyer before the payoff is settled leave a gap in which a judgment or a second sale could be filed first. Ask whoever handles your closing to confirm the recording time and to give you a copy showing the book and page.

sections.h2: How do mailed recordings, plats and payments work in Onslow County?
sections.html:
Mail is accepted if you include a self-addressed stamped envelope so the office can return the original. Checks go to Onslow County Register of Deeds for the exact amount due.

  • Business checks need a physical address and phone number.
  • Personal checks also need the driver license number and issuing state of the person writing the check.
  • Vital record requests take cash or money order only.
  • Plats can be e-submitted through approved vendors since May 1, 2021, or recorded in person. Paper or mylar at 18 by 24 inches is required, and sticky notes must stay off wet-ink seals.

If a plat has sticky residue, the office will reject it. That detail trips up owners who are dividing a lot before a sale.

sections.h2: What does Onslow County look like for home sellers?
sections.html:
Onslow County is a large, growing coastal county. The Census Bureau estimates 217,175 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 6.2% from the April 2020 base, on 762.08 square miles of land with 91,470 housing units.

For 2020 to 2024 the Bureau reports a 63.7% owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied home value of $236,400 and median gross rent of $1,265 across 75,265 households. It also counts 25,185 veterans, which shapes the buyer pool and the demand for rentals. These numbers describe the county as a whole, so a house in Jacksonville and one in a rural corner can sell very differently.

sections.h2: What if there is a lien, mortgage or back tax on the house?
sections.html:
Pay them off at closing and record the release. Satisfactions of a deed of trust are filed with no recording fee, so the lender's release costs the seller nothing at this office.

Property tax is a lien on the parcel from the date the property is listed each year, and interest starts after the due-date window in January. For a current payoff figure, ask the Onslow County Tax Office for your bill and any delinquent balance before you pick a closing date. If you owe more than the house will bring, speak with a closing attorney early, since a recorded lien must be cleared before a clean deed can pass to a buyer.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Onslow County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 602 Anne Street in Jacksonville, NC 28540, and mail goes to 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville. Call 910-347-3451 to confirm anything before you travel with an original deed.

faqs.q: Does Onslow County charge a fee to record a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. A general instrument is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each added page under the statewide schedule. Onslow County adds $10 per extra instrument in one document and a 3% processing fee on card payments of $5 or more.

faqs.q: Does the seller or buyer pay the excise tax in Onslow County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The transferor pays the register of deeds before recording, at the rate of $1 for each $500 or fractional part of the value conveyed.

faqs.q: Can the Onslow County office do a title search for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot perform title searches or help complete legal forms. They can show you the public records, and a closing attorney or title company can do the search.

faqs.q: What goes on the first page of a deed recorded in Onslow County?
faqs.a: The excise tax amount, including zero where nothing is due, and the legal reason if the transfer is exempt. The county also asks for a Tax Certification Form attached to the back of the original deed.
